source_title: BB Squeeze Breakout — Indicator by Alpha_Wizard
original_claim_summary: Author describes markets moving through a compression phase (Bollinger Bands narrow) followed by an expansion phase where volatility increases and a directional move can start; the indicator flags breakout bars with confirmation filters (RSI, volume, OBV, MACD, bandwidth) after price closes outside the bands for a required number of consecutive bars.
claimed_mechanism: Periods of contracting price range/volatility (narrowing Bollinger Bands) are followed by an expansion phase in which volatility increases and a directional move begins.
context: General technical/chart-agnostic context; author warns signals can fail in ranging, low-liquidity, high-spread, or news-driven conditions.
prerequisite_state: Bollinger Bands narrowed relative to recent history (compression/squeeze state) with declining bandwidth.
event_sequence: EVENT A: Bollinger Bandwidth contracts to a multi-bar low (squeeze) -> transition: price closes outside the bands for N consecutive bars with volume/momentum confirmation -> EVENT B: expansion phase begins, volatility rises and a directional move follows.
trigger: Close outside Bollinger Bands for a required number of consecutive bars, confirmed by RSI momentum, volume expansion, OBV slope, MACD behavior, and Bollinger Bandwidth expansion.
invalidation: Failure of price to sustain the close beyond the bands, or a signal firing in ranging/low-liquidity/high-spread/news-driven conditions per the author's own disclaimer.
claimed_outcome: A stronger, more sustained directional move (breakout) following the compression phase, categorized into BUY/SELL/WEAK BUY/WEAK SELL/WAIT signal strength.
falsification_condition: If measured post-squeeze (post-compression) realized volatility/expansion moves showed no statistically higher continuation or follow-through than random comparable non-squeeze periods, the claim would be false.

source_title: BB Squeeze Breakout — Indicator by Alpha_Wizard
original_claim_summary: The script's logic implies not every squeeze release turns into a sustained trend: it separates a 'post-squeeze context' state so a release with weak confirming volume/momentum is treated differently from one with strong confirmation, using signal tiers (BUY vs WEAK BUY) and warning that some breakouts fail.
claimed_mechanism: A breakout out of a volatility squeeze is only reliable when confirmed by concurrent momentum/volume expansion; unconfirmed squeeze releases frequently fail and the market re-enters a compressed/ranging state.
context: Applies after an already-identified compression/squeeze state; author notes conditions are worse in ranging, low-liquidity, high-spread or news-driven markets.
prerequisite_state: Price has already broken out of a Bollinger Band squeeze (an initial release has occurred).
event_sequence: EVENT A: initial squeeze release (close outside bands) -> transition: momentum/volume/OBV/MACD/bandwidth are checked for confirmation -> EVENT B: the move is classified as strong (BUY/SELL) or weak (WEAK BUY/WEAK SELL), or the setup is invalidated (WAIT) if the release lacks confirmation and price falls back inside the bands.
trigger: Confirmed vs. unconfirmed momentum/volume signature accompanying the initial band break.
invalidation: Price closes back inside the Bollinger Bands after the initial release (failed breakout / re-compression).
claimed_outcome: Confirmed releases are more likely to sustain a directional move; unconfirmed releases are more likely to fail and revert into range.
falsification_condition: If breakout follow-through rates (measured forward return / MFE) were statistically indistinguishable between 'confirmed' and 'unconfirmed' squeeze releases, the claim that confirmation predicts follow-through would be false.

source_title: Apollo: VWAP Rejection Indicator by InvestiShare
original_claim_summary: The author frames VWAP as a level institutional traders defend during trend pullbacks; when price touches VWAP, prints a doji (slowdown), and is followed by an engulfing candle with a volume spike in the trend direction, this is read as a continuation signal rather than a reversal.
claimed_mechanism: During an established trend, pullbacks to VWAP tend to attract defensive institutional order flow, causing price to slow down (doji) and then resume in the prevailing trend direction rather than reverse.
context: Trending market where price is positioned correctly relative to a 200-period EMA (i.e., a trend filter must agree with the signal direction).
prerequisite_state: Price above (for longs) or below (for shorts) the 200-period EMA, establishing directional bias, prior to the VWAP touch.
event_sequence: EVENT A: price pulls back and touches VWAP (wick or body) -> transition: the touching candle prints as a doji, signaling slowdown -> EVENT B: the next candle engulfs in the trend direction with a volume spike, confirming continuation.
trigger: Doji at VWAP touch followed by a same-direction engulfing candle exceeding a user-defined volume threshold.
invalidation: No engulfing follow-through, or the engulfing candle forms against the prevailing trend direction; price closing decisively through VWAP against the trend.
claimed_outcome: Price resumes the pre-pullback trend direction after the VWAP rejection, rather than reversing.
falsification_condition: If, across many instances of a doji-at-VWAP followed by a trend-direction engulfing candle plus volume spike, the forward continuation rate were no better than a random pullback baseline, the claim would be false.

source_title: Apollo: VWAP Rejection Indicator by InvestiShare
original_claim_summary: The indicator requires simultaneous alignment of a 200-period EMA trend filter with the VWAP-touch/doji/engulfing/volume pattern, implying the VWAP rejection pattern alone is not treated as sufficient and must agree with the higher-timeframe trend bias.
claimed_mechanism: A VWAP touch/rejection signal is more reliable as a trend-continuation trigger when it aligns with a higher-timeframe directional filter (price on the correct side of a 200-period EMA) than when taken in isolation.
context: Intraday/swing trending conditions where a longer moving average defines directional bias.
prerequisite_state: Price already positioned on the trend side of the 200 EMA before any VWAP touch is considered.
event_sequence: EVENT A: price sits on the trend side of the 200 EMA (bias established) -> transition: VWAP touch + doji + engulfing + volume filter all align with that bias -> EVENT B: the signal is taken; if price is on the wrong side of the 200 EMA, the same VWAP touch pattern is disregarded.
trigger: Simultaneous alignment of EMA-side positioning with the VWAP rejection pattern (all conditions cited in the script).
invalidation: EMA and VWAP-touch signals disagree (price beyond the EMA filter is inconsistent with the VWAP rejection direction).
claimed_outcome: Signals filtered by trend agreement are more trustworthy than VWAP-touch patterns taken without the EMA filter.
falsification_condition: If VWAP-touch continuation signals taken without any EMA trend filter performed no worse (equal win rate/expectancy) than those filtered by the 200 EMA, the added value of the trend filter claim would be false.

source_title: Kaufman Efficiency Ratio Gate [NovaLens] — Indicator by NovaLens
instrument: XAUUSD (gold), author states parameters generalize to other assets
original_claim_summary: The indicator computes Kaufman's Efficiency Ratio (net directional move divided by total path length over N bars) and classifies the market as trend-favorable when the ratio is high versus chop-dominant when it is low, with parameters tuned on gold price data.
claimed_mechanism: The ratio of net directional price change to the sum of absolute bar-to-bar price changes over a lookback window measures what fraction of price movement was 'efficient' (directional) versus noise; values near 1 indicate a trending regime and values near 0 indicate a choppy/range-bound regime.
context: General regime-classification context, tuned by the author using gold (XAUUSD) price data and claimed to generalize to other assets.
prerequisite_state: At least roughly 50-100 bars of price history available to compute a stable ratio.
event_sequence: EVENT A: efficiency ratio computed over N bars -> transition: value compared against a rolling median/threshold -> EVENT B: regime classified as trend-favorable (gate open) or chop-dominant (gate closed).
trigger: Efficiency ratio crossing above/below its rolling median threshold.
invalidation: None explicit; author states the metric is backward-looking and doesn't guarantee the next bar continues the classified regime.
claimed_outcome: Trend-following signals should be more reliable when the gate is open (high ER); mean-reversion or no-trade approaches are more appropriate when the gate is closed (low ER).
falsification_condition: If forward returns/volatility-adjusted performance of trend-following systems showed no improvement when gated by high-ER periods versus low-ER periods (on the same instrument and sample), the regime-utility claim would be false.

source_title: Kaufman Efficiency Ratio Gate [NovaLens] — Indicator by NovaLens
original_claim_summary: The description suggests using the efficiency ratio to switch strategy families: trend-following systems should be favored when the market is efficient/trending (high ER) and mean-reversion systems should be favored when the market is noisy/choppy (low ER).
claimed_mechanism: Trend-following strategies perform better when the efficiency ratio is high (low noise / genuine trending), while mean-reversion strategies perform better when the efficiency ratio is low (high noise / choppy, range-bound conditions); using the 'wrong' strategy type for the prevailing regime underperforms.
context: Regime-switching or strategy-selection frameworks that condition strategy choice on measured trendiness.
prerequisite_state: A computed efficiency ratio value for the current lookback window is available before deciding which strategy family to activate.
event_sequence: EVENT A: efficiency ratio computed -> transition: compared to a threshold to classify noise level -> EVENT B: a trend-following module is activated when ER is high; a mean-reversion module is activated when ER is low.
trigger: Efficiency ratio crossing a chosen noise threshold.
invalidation: Regime persists but the selected strategy type underperforms anyway (e.g., a 'trending' market by ER measure that whipsaws due to gaps or news).
claimed_outcome: Matching strategy type to the ER-defined regime avoids running trend systems in choppy markets and mean-reversion systems in trending markets, improving overall system performance.
falsification_condition: If trend-following systems did not underperform mean-reversion systems in low-ER regimes (and vice versa) when tested out of sample, the strategy-regime matching claim would be false.

source_title: Advanced Market Profile - Automated Volume Profile Indicator by iMetaX
timeframe: Intraday relative to prior daily session
original_claim_summary: The script documents the classic market-profile '80% rule': if price opens outside yesterday's value area, pushes back inside, and is accepted, there is a claimed 80% probability it rotates completely to the other side of the value area, and the indicator auto-generates take-profit targets from this rule.
claimed_mechanism: When price opens outside the prior day's value area, pushes back inside it, and is accepted (closes, not just wicks, beyond the boundary), the market has a claimed 80% historical probability of rotating completely across to the opposite edge of the value area.
context: Applies at session open relative to the prior day's value area (68-70% volume zone) in market-profile-style analysis; presumes a defined 'yesterday' session boundary (e.g., futures/equity index products with clear daily sessions).
prerequisite_state: Current session opens outside the previous day's value area (above VAH or below VAL).
event_sequence: EVENT A: session opens outside prior day's value area -> transition: price pushes back inside the value area and closes beyond the boundary (acceptance, not a wick) -> EVENT B: price rotates across the entire value area to the opposite edge.
trigger: A confirmed close-based acceptance back inside the value area after an outside open (not merely an intraday wick touch).
invalidation: Price only wicks into the value area without closing beyond the boundary (rejection, not acceptance); price re-exits back outside the value area shortly after re-entry.
claimed_outcome: Full rotation across the value area to the opposite edge, used to set take-profit targets.
falsification_condition: If, across a large reproducible sample of instances where price opened outside and was re-accepted inside the prior day's value area, the rate of full rotation to the opposite edge were materially below 80% (e.g., close to a coin-flip or lower), the claim would be false.

source_title: Advanced Market Profile - Automated Volume Profile Indicator by iMetaX
original_claim_summary: The indicator distinguishes a brief wick beyond a structural level from a true close-based break, stating a quick wick doesn't signal acceptance while a close beyond structural levels confirms a real break, tying this to whether price rotates back toward the point of control or continues.
claimed_mechanism: A brief wick beyond a value-area or structural boundary does not constitute genuine market acceptance of that price; only a close beyond the level indicates a real shift in where the market is willing to transact, and only true acceptance should be treated as confirming a breakout/trend continuation.
context: Any breakout-acceptance framework built on market-profile value area or similar structural levels.
prerequisite_state: Price approaches or briefly trades beyond a defined structural boundary (value area edge, point of control, prior range extreme).
event_sequence: EVENT A: price wicks beyond the boundary intraday -> transition: the bar/period closes back on the original side (rejection) or closes beyond the level (acceptance) -> EVENT B: rejection favors reversion into the range (toward the point of control); acceptance favors trend continuation beyond the level.
trigger: Close price relative to the structural boundary at bar/period close, not intrabar wick extremes.
invalidation: A close beyond the level followed shortly by price failing back inside would indicate the 'acceptance' read was wrong (a false acceptance).
claimed_outcome: Rejections rotate price back toward the point of control/range middle; acceptances lead to continuation beyond the broken level.
falsification_condition: If close-based 'acceptance' events beyond a structural boundary led to continuation no more often than wick-only 'rejection' events reverted, the distinction between acceptance and rejection would carry no predictive value and the claim would be false.

source_title: Fair Value Gap Fill Probability [PickMyTrade] — Indicator by PickMyTrade_Official
original_claim_summary: The indicator identifies three-candle fair value gaps and claims that while unfilled, these zones can act as support or resistance, drawing price back to fill the imbalance before continuing or reversing.
claimed_mechanism: A three-candle price imbalance (a gap where consecutive candle wicks do not overlap) represents an area the market traded through inefficiently; while unfilled, this zone can act as support (bullish FVG) or resistance (bearish FVG), and price is drawn back to it to 'fill' the imbalance before continuing or reversing.
context: Any market/timeframe where a 3-candle non-overlapping range can be identified; typically used in intraday/swing price-action-based (ICT-style) frameworks.
prerequisite_state: A 3-candle sequence exists where the 1st and 3rd candle's wicks do not overlap, exceeding a minimum ATR-based size filter.
event_sequence: EVENT A: a 3-candle imbalance forms (gap) -> transition: price later returns toward the gap zone -> EVENT B: price reacts (support/resistance) at the gap edge, or trades through it entirely (fill), each read as a different signal.
trigger: Price re-entering the identified FVG zone (top/bottom/midpoint boundaries).
invalidation: Price fully trades through the gap (breaks the opposite boundary), which the framework treats as invalidation/removal of the zone as an active support/resistance level.
claimed_outcome: Reaction/reversal at the gap edge, or a full fill followed by a reversal/continuation depending on interpretation.
falsification_condition: If price reactions (bounces/reversals) at identified FVG zones occurred no more frequently than at randomly chosen equivalent-sized price zones on the same chart, the support/resistance claim for FVGs would be false.

source_title: Fair Value Gap Fill Probability [PickMyTrade] — Indicator by PickMyTrade_Official
original_claim_summary: The indicator applies a Gaussian Naive Bayes classifier using CVD momentum, gap-size-relative-to-ATR, and time-at-price features to output a relative fill-probability score per fair value gap, learned online from the chart's own history, while cautioning the scores are not calibrated probabilities.
claimed_mechanism: The likelihood that a given fair value gap will be filled before it expires is not fixed but varies systematically with measurable features -- cumulative volume delta momentum, the gap's size relative to recent ATR, and how much time price has spent near the gap -- allowing a statistical/ML classifier to output a relative fill-probability score per gap.
context: Any instrument with volume or volume-proxy (CVD) data available; the author explicitly cautions the CVD estimator is 'synthetic and noisier on illiquid symbols.'
prerequisite_state: An identified, still-open (unfilled) FVG with its associated gap-geometry and volume-derived features computed.
event_sequence: EVENT A: FVG identified and features computed (CVD momentum, gap/ATR ratio, time-at-price) -> transition: a Gaussian Naive Bayes classifier scores the gap -> EVENT B: the gap is later observed to fill (price reaches midpoint) or expires unfilled, which is used as the outcome label.
trigger: Feature values crossing whatever internal thresholds the online-learning classifier has established from prior labeled gaps on the same chart.
invalidation: The author explicitly states the scores are 'relative confidence, not calibrated frequentist probabilities' and 'historically associated with, not predictive of, future behaviour' -- i.e., the model does not claim forward-looking calibration.
claimed_outcome: Higher-scored gaps fill more often than lower-scored gaps within the same dataset/chart history.
falsification_condition: If gaps scored as high fill-probability by the classifier filled no more often than gaps scored low, in an out-of-sample test withheld from the online learner, the claim that these features predict fill likelihood would be false.

source_title: Volatility Compression Breakout — Indicator by LeafAlgo
instrument: generic/multi (author states it applies to any financial instrument and timeframe)
original_claim_summary: The indicator identifies periods of low volatility (price consolidating near the Keltner midline and an EMA) followed by potential breakout opportunities, coloring bars bullish, neutral, or bearish based on whether the close is above, between, or below both lines.
claimed_mechanism: Periods where price consolidates in a narrow range near the Keltner Channel midline and an EMA (low realized volatility) precede periods of expanded directional price movement once price closes decisively above or below both lines.
context: Any instrument/timeframe per the author ('can be applied to any financial instrument and timeframe').
prerequisite_state: Price trading between/near the Keltner midline and EMA in a narrow, low-volatility band (neutral/yellow state).
event_sequence: EVENT A: price consolidates near the Keltner mid and EMA (neutral state) -> transition: price closes decisively above or below both lines -> EVENT B: a directional (bullish/bearish) move follows with expanded volatility.
trigger: Close above both the Keltner middle line and EMA (bullish) or close below both (bearish).
invalidation: Price closes back between the two lines shortly after a directional signal (false breakout, reversion to neutral state).
claimed_outcome: A sustained directional move following the compression phase.
falsification_condition: If forward realized volatility/directional persistence following a compression-to-breakout signal were statistically indistinguishable from randomly sampled non-signal periods on the same instrument, the claim would be false.

source_title: simple-crypto-breakout-strategy
original_claim_summary: The repo implements a breakout strategy based on the previous day's trading range, described as popularized by Larry Williams, entering on a limit order at the range-derived threshold and closing all positions by end of day; backtested on ETH-PERP for 2020.
claimed_mechanism: A breakout beyond a threshold derived from the previous day's trading range signals the start of an intraday momentum move worth trading in the breakout direction, an approach popularized by Larry Williams' volatility breakout method.
context: Cryptocurrency perpetual futures (tested on ETH-PERP); intraday, single-session holding.
prerequisite_state: The previous day's high-low range has been computed to define breakout thresholds for the new session.
event_sequence: EVENT A: the previous day's range establishes upper/lower threshold levels -> transition: price breaks through a limit order set at the threshold during the new session -> EVENT B: the position is held intraday and closed at end of day regardless of outcome.
trigger: Price reaching the previous-day-range-derived limit order level.
invalidation: The position is time-stopped at end of day irrespective of whether the move continued; a 2% stop loss also invalidates the trade if the breakout fails immediately.
claimed_outcome: Directional continuation intraday following the breakout, captured before a forced end-of-day exit.
claimed_horizon: Intraday (single session, closed by end of day)
falsification_condition: If the strategy's reported 304.7% return and -7.23% max drawdown over 2020 on ETH-PERP failed to replicate directionally (e.g., produced negative or benchmark-lagging risk-adjusted returns) on an out-of-sample period or a different crypto asset, the breakout-continuation edge claim would be false.

source_title: simple-crypto-breakout-strategy
original_claim_summary: The strategy forces every breakout position closed at end of day rather than holding overnight, which the reported backtest associates with a much smaller max drawdown (-7.23%) than a buy-and-hold benchmark (-61.45%) over the same period.
claimed_mechanism: Forcing exit of breakout positions by the end of the trading day, rather than holding overnight, is claimed to control risk on breakout trades by avoiding adverse multi-day reversion or gap risk that could erase the intraday breakout gains.
context: 24/7 crypto markets where 'end of day' is an arbitrary but consistently applied cutoff (no exchange close), used as a risk-management discipline.
prerequisite_state: An open breakout position that has not yet hit its stop loss during the session.
event_sequence: EVENT A: a breakout position is opened intraday -> transition: the session/day elapses without the stop loss being hit -> EVENT B: the position is force-closed at end of day regardless of unrealized P&L.
trigger: End-of-day time cutoff.
invalidation: None stated beyond the stop loss; the exit is unconditional on time.
claimed_outcome: Reported backtest max drawdown (-7.23%) is much smaller than buy-and-hold max drawdown (-61.45%) over the same period, attributed partly to this time-based risk control.
falsification_condition: If removing the end-of-day forced exit (allowing positions to run) produced a lower max drawdown or higher risk-adjusted return than the time-stopped version over the same data, the claimed risk-control benefit of the end-of-day exit would be false.

source_title: quant-trading (je-suis-tm) — London Breakout strategy
original_claim_summary: The London Breakout strategy uses the price range of the hour before the London FX session opens (GMT 7:00-7:59) as breakout thresholds, trading in the direction of a breach once London opens, on the premise that the Tokyo-to-London liquidity handover creates a directional opportunity.
claimed_mechanism: Because FX trading activity and liquidity shift as the Tokyo session closes and the London session opens, the price range established in the hour just before London's open (a lower-liquidity transition window) tends to be broken directionally once London's higher liquidity arrives, making that pre-open range a usable breakout threshold.
context: FX currency pairs around the London session open (GMT 07:00-07:59 pre-open range used to set thresholds).
prerequisite_state: The GMT 07:00-07:59 pre-London-open hourly range has been established (high/low recorded).
event_sequence: EVENT A: the pre-London-open hour range is recorded -> transition: the London session opens and liquidity/participation increases -> EVENT B: price breaches the upper or lower threshold of the pre-open range, triggering a directional trade.
trigger: Price breaching the upper or lower bound of the pre-open-hour range after the London session opens.
invalidation: Price stays within the pre-open range through the session (no breakout materializes).
claimed_outcome: A directional move in the breakout direction as London session liquidity arrives.
falsification_condition: If breakouts of the pre-London-open range showed no directional persistence beyond what's expected from a random walk once transaction costs and slippage are included, the London-session liquidity-transition claim would be false.

source_title: quant-trading (je-suis-tm) — Dual Thrust strategy
instrument: generic/multi (intraday instruments with a defined daily session)
original_claim_summary: The Dual Thrust strategy computes upper/lower breakout thresholds from the prior day's open, high, low and close, entering in the breakout direction, reversing on an opposite-threshold breach, and liquidating all positions by day end.
claimed_mechanism: Setting asymmetric upper/lower breakout thresholds from the prior day's open, high, low, and close captures the market's recent range/imbalance; a price move beyond those thresholds after the new session opens signals the start of a directional move worth trading, with a same-day reversal or close-out if the opposite threshold is later breached.
context: Intraday trading on instruments with a defined daily open/close structure.
prerequisite_state: The prior day's OHLC data is available to compute the day's upper and lower breakout thresholds before the new session opens.
event_sequence: EVENT A: thresholds are computed from the prior day's OHLC range at session open -> transition: price exceeds the upper or lower threshold intraday -> EVENT B: a position is entered in the breakout direction; positions reverse if price later crosses to the opposite threshold and are liquidated by day's end.
trigger: Price crossing the computed upper/lower threshold intraday.
invalidation: Price remains between the thresholds all session (no trade), or reverses to the opposite threshold (position flip).
claimed_outcome: A capturable directional move for the remainder of the session following threshold breach.
falsification_condition: If Dual Thrust threshold breakouts produced returns statistically indistinguishable from a random intraday entry benchmark once realistic costs are applied, the claimed opening-range-breakout edge would be false.

source_title: quant-trading (je-suis-tm) — Pair Trading strategy
original_claim_summary: The Pair Trading strategy uses Engle-Granger cointegration to identify related stock pairs, standardizes the residual spread, and trades a long/short position when the residual exceeds a one-sigma two-tailed threshold, expecting reversion toward the historical equilibrium spread.
claimed_mechanism: Two stocks that are statistically cointegrated (via Engle-Granger analysis) share a long-run equilibrium spread; when their standardized residual spread deviates beyond a one-sigma threshold, it is expected to revert, so buying the relatively cheap leg and shorting the relatively expensive leg captures the reversion.
context: Equity pairs identified as cointegrated over a lookback window; the author notes the cointegration relationship 'breaks sooner or later,' requiring ongoing monitoring.
prerequisite_state: A pair of instruments confirmed cointegrated via the Engle-Granger test over the estimation window.
event_sequence: EVENT A: cointegration relationship established and residual spread standardized -> transition: standardized residual exceeds a one-sigma (two-tailed) threshold -> EVENT B: long the underperforming leg / short the outperforming leg, expecting the spread to revert toward zero.
trigger: Standardized residual crossing the one-sigma threshold.
invalidation: The cointegration relationship breaks down (residual continues diverging rather than reverting, or the statistical relationship fails re-testing).
claimed_outcome: The spread reverts toward its historical mean, generating profit on the long/short pair position.
falsification_condition: If the standardized spread of a cointegrated pair failed to revert toward its historical mean after crossing the one-sigma threshold more often than chance across many independent pair-periods, the mean-reversion claim would be false.

source_title: quant-trading (je-suis-tm) — Awesome Oscillator strategy
original_claim_summary: The Awesome Oscillator strategy derives momentum from moving averages of the bar midpoint (High+Low)/2 rather than close, and claims a 'saucer' pattern in the histogram signals a resuming trend earlier than waiting for a MACD-style crossover, tested against MACD as a control.
claimed_mechanism: Momentum derived from the difference between a short and long moving average of the bar midpoint ((High+Low)/2), rather than closing price, tends to cluster in the same direction during trends and oscillate near zero during consolidation; a 'saucer' pattern (a dip-and-recovery shape in the histogram) is claimed to signal a resuming trend earlier than waiting for a MACD-style crossover/divergence.
context: Equities, tested against MACD as a comparative control to assess relative timing/outperformance.
prerequisite_state: An existing directional bias (the histogram is already same-colored/same-sign) before a saucer pattern is looked for.
event_sequence: EVENT A: the oscillator histogram is in a directional (colored) state -> transition: the histogram forms a saucer (dip and recovery in the same direction without crossing zero) -> EVENT B: the trend resumes, generating an earlier entry than a MACD crossover would provide.
trigger: Saucer pattern formation in the histogram while it remains on one side of zero.
invalidation: The histogram crosses to the opposite side of zero (the trend outright reverses rather than pausing).
claimed_outcome: Earlier trend-resumption entries than MACD-based signals, with directional performance compared against a MACD control.
falsification_condition: If saucer-pattern entries did not produce earlier or better risk-adjusted results than MACD crossover entries across the tested equities, the claimed timing advantage would be false.

source_title: freqtrade-strategies (SilvanStrategy) — Alessandro Arrabito
instrument: Binance USDT-margined perpetual futures: XRP, BNB, SOL, TRX, DOGE, ADA, LINK, AVAX
original_claim_summary: SilvanStrategy conditions altcoin trend-following versus mean-reversion logic on whether Bitcoin trades above or below its own moving average, but the author explicitly built and disclosed the repo as an educational demonstration that this apparent edge is manufactured via curve-fitting, survivorship bias, and a hindsight-tuned regime filter.
claimed_mechanism: Bitcoin's price relative to its own moving average is used as a market-wide regime filter: when BTC is above its moving average (risk-on/trending regime), altcoin perpetuals are traded with trend-following logic; when BTC is below it (risk-off), mean-reversion logic is applied instead, on the premise that altcoin behavior is conditioned by the broader BTC-driven crypto market regime.
context: Binance USDT-margined perpetual futures on a fixed set of altcoins (XRP, BNB, SOL, TRX, DOGE, ADA, LINK, AVAX), 2020-2026 backtest period.
prerequisite_state: BTC price and its moving average are both computed to classify the prevailing regime before any altcoin signal is acted on.
event_sequence: EVENT A: BTC regime is classified via its position relative to its own moving average -> transition: an altcoin trend or mean-reversion module is activated depending on the BTC regime -> EVENT B: a trade is taken in the altcoin using the regime-appropriate signal type.
trigger: BTC crossing its regime-defining moving average.
invalidation: The author explicitly demonstrates this invalidates itself out of sample: walk-forward testing shows CAGR collapsing to -13.61% to 4.60% versus an in-sample 35-107%, i.e., the regime filter (its specific EMA length in particular) was tuned with hindsight and does not generalize.
claimed_outcome: In-sample: +983% total return, 68.3% win rate, Sharpe 1.48. Out-of-sample/walk-forward: near-total collapse of the edge, demonstrating the regime-filter mechanism as documented does not generalize.
falsification_condition: This mechanism's validity is already falsified by the author's own walk-forward test: out-of-sample CAGR (-13.61% to 4.60%) far below in-sample (35-107%) demonstrates the BTC-regime-conditioned trend/mean-reversion split does not generalize beyond the fitted period.

source_title: freqtrade-strategies (SilvanStrategy) — Alessandro Arrabito
instrument: Binance USDT-margined perpetual futures: XRP, BNB, SOL, TRX, DOGE, ADA, LINK, AVAX
original_claim_summary: The author documents that using a static pairlist of coins already known to have performed well over the backtest period (rather than a point-in-time-accurate universe) is one of five intentional flaws inflating the strategy's apparent historical performance.
claimed_mechanism: Building a backtest around a fixed list of assets that are already known (at the time of building the backtest) to have performed well over the backtest period systematically inflates the strategy's apparent historical performance, because assets that would have been dropped or delisted for poor performance are excluded from consideration.
context: Any multi-asset systematic strategy backtest using a static, hand-picked instrument universe rather than a point-in-time-accurate universe.
prerequisite_state: A static pairlist/universe was chosen using information available after the backtest period ends (look-ahead in universe construction).
event_sequence: EVENT A: a universe is selected using post-hoc knowledge of which assets performed well -> transition: a backtest is run over the historical period using this fixed universe -> EVENT B: the reported aggregate performance is inflated relative to what a point-in-time-honest universe selection would have produced.
claimed_outcome: Reported backtest returns overstate what a real-time, point-in-time-honest version of the strategy would have achieved.
falsification_condition: If a point-in-time-accurate (survivorship-bias-free) universe reconstruction produced performance statistically similar to the static-pairlist backtest, the survivorship-bias inflation claim would be false.

source_title: ATR-breakout-strategy
instrument: US large-cap equities (S&P 500 + Nasdaq-100 plus liquid extras, filtered to top ~223 names by 60-day dollar volume)
original_claim_summary: The strategy enters when a stock's daily high pierces a volatility-adjusted Keltner-style upper band (EMA(20) + 3x ATR(20)) while the broad market (SPY) is above its 200-day moving average, ranks candidates by 63-day momentum, and exits via a trailing ATR stop or a 10-day-low breach.
claimed_mechanism: In liquid large-cap equities already in an established uptrend (price above its 200-day moving average), a new high that pierces a volatility-adjusted upper band (prior day's EMA(20) + 3x ATR(20)) signals genuine momentum follow-through worth entering, rather than noise, because the move exceeds several multiples of the recent typical daily range.
context: US large-cap equities (S&P 500 + Nasdaq-100 plus liquid extras, filtered to the top ~223 names by 60-day dollar volume, rebuilt weekly); trades only taken when the broad market (SPY) is above its 200-day moving average.
prerequisite_state: Both the stock and the broad market (SPY) are above their 200-day moving averages; the stock has sufficient liquidity to be in the top dollar-volume universe.
event_sequence: EVENT A: the stock's prior-day EMA(20)+3xATR(20) band is computed -> transition: today's high pierces that band -> EVENT B: a position is entered, ranked among concurrent signals by 63-day trailing momentum, and held until a trailing ATR stop or a close below the prior 10-day low fires.
trigger: Today's high price exceeding yesterday's EMA(20) + 3.0x ATR(20) band level, with SPY above its 200-day moving average.
invalidation: Price closes below the prior 10-day low, or a trailing stop at (highest close since entry) - 1.5x ATR(14) is hit.
claimed_outcome: Follow-through continuation of the breakout, captured via the position until a volatility-based trailing stop or a structural low breach exits it.
claimed_horizon: Multi-day to multi-week (position held until a trailing stop or 10-day-low breach)
falsification_condition: If stocks piercing the EMA(20)+3xATR(20) band while above their 200-day MA showed no better forward returns than a random entry in the same uptrending universe, the momentum-follow-through claim would be false.

source_title: cute-intraday-option-strats (c36_vwap_mr_option_native_quality_v1)
instrument: SPY, QQQ (expressed via 0-2 DTE single-leg options)
original_claim_summary: The documented VWAP mean-reversion model computes a rolling z-score of the close-minus-VWAP residual and enters when the z-score recovers from an extreme deviation (<= -1.35, mirrored for shorts) back above -0.65 on a confirming reversal candle, expressing the trade via short-dated SPY/QQQ options.
claimed_mechanism: Intraday price deviations from the session's volume-weighted average price, measured as a rolling z-score of the close-minus-VWAP residual, tend to revert back toward VWAP once the deviation reaches a statistically extreme level and then begins recovering, particularly when confirmed by a same-direction reversal candle.
context: Liquid U.S. index ETFs (SPY, QQQ) intraday, 0-2 DTE options used to express the signal; a hard session cutoff at 3:55pm ET is enforced.
prerequisite_state: A rolling 20-bar standard deviation of the VWAP residual has been computed to normalize the current deviation into a z-score.
event_sequence: EVENT A: the VWAP residual z-score drops to <= -1.35 (or rises symmetrically for shorts) -> transition: the z-score recovers back above -0.65 on a bar that also closes higher than it opened -> EVENT B: entry is executed on the next bar's open, targeting reversion back toward VWAP.
trigger: z_prev <= -1.35 and z_now >= -0.65, combined with a bullish (or mirrored bearish) signal candle.
invalidation: Stop loss hit; an opposite-color candle after a minimum 3-minute hold; a 25-minute maximum time budget elapses; or the 3:55pm ET session cutoff is reached.
claimed_outcome: Price reverts toward VWAP, monetized via short-dated options; reported evaluation shows +16004 PnL over 15 trades with a Deflated Sharpe Ratio of 0.64.
falsification_condition: If the VWAP residual z-score reversion entries (z_prev <= -1.35 recovering above -0.65 with a signal candle) failed to show positive expectancy after Deflated Sharpe Ratio correction on new out-of-sample SPY/QQQ data, the mean-reversion mechanism claim would be false.

source_title: cute-intraday-option-strats (c36_vwap_mr_option_native_quality_v1)
instrument: SPY, QQQ (expressed via 0-2 DTE single-leg options)
timeframe: Intraday, up to 25 minutes per trade
original_claim_summary: The model imposes a 25-minute maximum holding time and a hard 3:55pm ET cutoff on top of stop-loss/target exits, on the premise that mean-reversion signals decay and late-session risk rises the longer a position is held without the expected reversion occurring.
claimed_mechanism: Intraday mean-reversion signals decay in reliability the longer a position is held without the expected reversion occurring, and the risk of being caught in an adverse move increases near the session close; imposing a maximum holding time (25 minutes) and a hard cutoff before end-of-day (3:55pm ET) is claimed to limit exposure to these decaying/late-session risks better than an open-ended hold.
context: 0-2 DTE options on liquid index ETFs, where time decay (theta) and end-of-day volatility/liquidity changes are pronounced.
prerequisite_state: An open mean-reversion position that has not yet reached its target or stop.
event_sequence: EVENT A: a position is opened on a reversion signal -> transition: the position ages toward the 25-minute budget or the session approaches 3:55pm ET without the target being hit -> EVENT B: the position is closed by the time/session cutoff regardless of unrealized P&L.
trigger: 25-minute elapsed hold time or the 3:55pm ET session clock.
invalidation: None beyond the time cutoffs themselves (they are unconditional).
claimed_outcome: Reduced tail risk from stale/failed reversion trades and from adverse late-session moves, contributing to the reported positive risk-adjusted (DSR-based) performance.
claimed_horizon: Up to 25 minutes, or end-of-day at 3:55pm ET
falsification_condition: If removing the 25-minute time-box and 3:55pm cutoff (allowing trades to run until target/stop only) produced equal or better risk-adjusted performance than the time-boxed version on the same data, the claimed benefit of the time-based exits would be false.
